i want to replace the classic auto-develop with SVDLUT — ICCV, here is part of my discussion w GPT-web 
---
| Model | Why it belongs on your shortlist | Available implementation | Expected integration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SVDLUT — ICCV 2025** | My first choice for the quality/footprint/speed compromise. Spatially aware, rather than just a global color LUT. | Official PyTorch implementation and pretrained models; Apache-2.0. | Export the predictor; port the fused LUT/grid application kernel. |
| **LLF-LUT++ — TPAMI, released 2025** | Most directly aligned with developing high-dynamic-range input into a pleasing image, including local detail and contrast. | Official code and pretrained checkpoints; MIT. | More work: LUT application plus multiscale pyramid processing. |
| **BPAM — ICCV 2025** | Another strong local-enhancement architecture: predicts tiny, spatially varying MLPs instead of one global transform. | Official PyTorch repository with a pretrained directory; MIT. | Grid slicing and per-pixel MLP application need careful GPU deployment. |
| **SepLUT — ECCV 2022** | Older, but a useful low-complexity baseline: learned 1D curves plus a 3D LUT. | Official pretrained sRGB and XYZ models; Apache-2.0. | Probably the easiest full-resolution rendering stage to port. |
I’ll check SVDLUT’s official code and pretrained models against our RAW/JPEG pipeline, including its input color space, GPU rendering path, and what replacing A would mean for Lightroom export.

The official implementation includes separate sRGB retouching and XYZ tone-mapping paths, so there’s a plausible fit for both JPEG and RAW. Its small predictor can be separated from the full-resolution GPU transform. [Official code](https://github.com/WontaeaeKim/SVDLUT)

The major tradeoff is Lightroom export: SVDLUT changes the same color differently depending on its position in the image. Our current global exposure/curve XMP cannot reproduce that. We need to decide how much matching Lightroom output matters before settling the replacement plan.

I found a significant issue in the released SVDLUT code: both CPU and CUDA kernels use integer division for spatial coordinates. Almost every pixel therefore samples the same spatial corner, undermining the advertised local adaptation. There’s an [open upstream report](https://github.com/WontaeaeKim/SVDLUT/issues/2) with no author response.

Simply correcting the division could change the behavior expected by the pretrained weights. I recommend comparing the released and corrected kernels on your photos before replacing A. The Lightroom plugin will remain deferred as requested.

# Replace classic A with SVDLUT

## Summary

Replace Basicadj auto-adjustment behind the existing **A** control with SVDLUT for RAW and JPEG development. Preserve independent AWB controls, automatic activation rules, lazy variants, and the existing RAW decode.

Finish will create a full-resolution TIFF for **kept captures with a RAW and A selected**. RAW sidecars retain AWB settings; the TIFF carries the SVDLUT appearance. Lightroom stacking and JPEG-only automatic handoff remain deferred.

## 1. Qualify the pretrained models first

- Pin official SVDLUT revision `4759030cb6a51641a97f4031f56bc21e032e5cea`, checkpoint hashes, and Apache-2.0 attribution. Evaluate the small `fiveK_XYZ` and `fiveK_sRGB` checkpoints; exclude the larger PPR10K models initially.
- Compare the released kernel against a corrected floating-point spatial-coordinate implementation. Preserve both in qualification tooling, not as user-facing modes. The released CPU/CUDA kernels have the [reported integer-division defect](https://github.com/WontaeaeKim/SVDLUT/issues/2).
- Establish the XYZ checkpoint’s white point, channel ordering, scaling, and clipping conventions from upstream data/reference outputs. Do not directly substitute our D50 XYZ intermediate without verifying the conversion.
- Compare Original, classic A, and both SVDLUT implementations on copied daylight, indoor, skin, mixed-light, sunset, underexposed, and highlight-heavy photographs. Include the previously problematic warm Sony RAWs and JPEG phone images.
- Present comparisons before the production switch. If corrected processing introduces systematic artifacts or the RAW input convention cannot be established, retain classic A and report the blocker. Retraining is outside this plan.

## 2. Native inference and rendering

- Export the predictor and table reconstruction to ONNX for existing DirectML inference. Run prediction from the upstream 256×256 input convention; port fused grid slicing/LUT application to WGSL.
- RAW processing retains black correction, selected white balance, highlight reconstruction, demosaic, and calibrated color conversion. SVDLUT replaces Basicadj’s automatic tone/color stage.
- JPEG processing uses normalized sRGB. When AWB is selected, apply its existing linear-light correction before returning to the model’s sRGB input domain.
- Preserve floating-point precision until final output; do not route RAW development through an intermediate 8-bit JPEG.
- Predict once per requested A/AWB combination and cache the resulting tables. Use identical parameters for thumbnails, full-resolution viewing, ranking, and TIFF output.
- Use full-image spatial coordinates across GPU bands and tiles. Orientation must agree between predictor input and rendering; viewport zoom must never rerun prediction on the cropped view.
- Reuse memory-budgeted concurrent GPU scheduling. Account for model sessions and rendering buffers, targeting the headless A4000 and an 8 GiB ceiling.

## 3. Recipes, compatibility, and controls

- Replace the Basicadj-only correction payload with a versioned treatment supporting legacy Basicadj recipes and SVDLUT tables, alongside the existing white-balance data.
- Include checkpoint, preprocessing, kernel revision, source identity, orientation, and AWB treatment in cache identities. Invalidate dependent previews and ranking evidence together.
- Preserve existing review choices and undo history. Regenerate outdated A artifacts lazily; never interpret legacy parameter bytes as SVDLUT data.
- Keep Original / A / AWB / A+AWB behavior. AWB still automatically accompanies automatic A activation, with neutral-AWB fallback when preference mapping fails.
- Surface inference failures without silently presenting classic output as successful SVDLUT development.

## 4. Finish and Lightroom

- Produce an upright, full-resolution **16-bit RGB TIFF with embedded sRGB profile and lossless compression**, named `<stem>-Autocull.tif`, using the selected cached recipe.
- TIFF pixels include A and, when selected, AWB. Preserve capture metadata and record source/model provenance; avoid embedding adjustments that would apply the development twice.
- RAW XMP exports the selected AWB only. Remove superseded Autocull-owned classic A settings while preserving unrelated metadata. Do not pretend SVDLUT’s spatial treatment is represented by global Lightroom sliders.
- Generate TIFFs only during Finish, with progress reporting and memory-bounded work. Decode the source once for that export; do not rerun prediction.
- Journal TIFF creation alongside existing Finish operations. Support interruption, retry, rollback, source-change checks, and collision-safe naming without overwriting unrelated files.
- Track generated TIFFs as derivatives so reopening the shoot does not introduce new culling candidates or repeated exports.
- JPEG-only photos and rejected captures receive no new TIFF. Ordinary Lightroom import can load the TIFF and originals, but automatic stacking requires the deferred plugin.

## Validation

- Check ONNX predictions and WGSL output against the qualified reference, including interpolation boundaries, spatial gradients, portrait orientation, and band seams.
- Verify all four control combinations, cache invalidation, legacy catalogs, single-decode development, and consistent preview/full-resolution/export recipes.
- Verify TIFF precision, profile, metadata, orientation, decoded-pixel agreement, and Finish recovery/collision behavior.
- Measure cold/warm latency and concurrent memory use headlessly on the A4000; label the 8 GiB ceiling separately from physical 8GB hardware testing.
- Run affected core, engine, renderer, and app tests plus strict workspace Clippy through the existing Windows/mbx build setup.
- Record qualification evidence and maintain the implementation ExecPlan under `.agents/plans/`.

I’ll check SVDLUT’s release history for a working spatial version, then inspect LLF-LUT++ and BPAM’s official code and checkpoints. The current evidence shows incompatible code and weights; it doesn’t establish how that happened.

There’s no older working SVDLUT version in the official history: all three commits use the same kernels and checkpoints. The later changes only adjust the training scheduler and add a video test.

BPAM looks like the better next candidate for our pipeline. It has separate retouching and tone-mapping checkpoints checked into the repo, and its reference implementation uses floating-point spatial coordinates. LLF-LUT++ is also viable, but its multiscale filtering adds more rendering and memory-management work. I’m checking the configurations before making a firm recommendation.

**No older working SVDLUT release turned up.** Its official history has only three commits; the kernels and checkpoints are unchanged since the initial release. Subsequent changes touched only the training scheduler and video testing. [History comparison](https://github.com/WontaeaeKim/SVDLUT/compare/47cd9707c818288b3b5d716512523d1e1ef092c6...4759030cb6a51641a97f4031f56bc21e032e5cea)

A release mistake is possible, but we can’t establish that. Because the published demo matches the buggy kernel, this is more than a recent typo we can safely fix. There’s still no response to the [upstream report](https://github.com/WontaeaeKim/SVDLUT/issues/2).

**I’d qualify BPAM next**, keeping LLF-LUT++ as the second candidate:

| | BPAM | LLF-LUT++ |
|---|---|---|
| Available weights | Separate retouching and tone-mapping checkpoints, directly in repo | TPAMI checkpoints linked externally |
| Spatial processing | Floating-point grid sampling in the reference code | Multiscale Laplacian filtering |
| Integration outlook | Better fit for our predictor + GPU rendering architecture | More pyramid processing, intermediate buffers, and boundary handling |

Sources: [BPAM implementation](https://github.com/CVL-UESTC/BPAM), [LLF-LUT++ implementation](https://github.com/fengzhang427/LLF-LUT).

That’s an integration recommendation, **not yet a quality verdict**. BPAM still needs the same reference-output, RAW color-space, and memory qualification before replacing A. Our AWB and TIFF-export decisions carry over.
